title: Loading the revolver
subtitle: Loading and unloading the revolver, right and left handed

lines: This episode teaches the correct method of loading and unloading the revolver.
We'll go step by step, first right-handed, then for a left-handed shooter.

scenes.heading: Loading the revolver
bullets: Identify a safe direction
Safe direction, finger off the trigger
Release the catch and open the cylinder
Moved to the right, cylinder controlled
Load the chambers, rotate with the thumb
Replace the grip with the gun hand
Make sure the cylinder is locked in place
The revolver is now ready to be fired
lines: Page forty six gives the steps for loading the revolver.

lines.text: Step one: identify a safe direction.
Step two: point the firearm in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger.
Step three: placing your support hand under the trigger guard and your right thumb on the cylinder, release the catch and open the cylinder.
Step four: notice how the firearm has been moved to the right and the cylinder is controlled.
Step five: load the ammunition into the chambers of the cylinder.

lines: The cylinder can be rotated with the thumb while loading.

lines.text: Step six: replace the grip with the gun hand.
Step seven: make sure the cylinder is locked in place.
Step eight: the revolver is now ready to be fired.

scenes.heading: Step three
scenes.caption: Loading, step 3: release the catch and open the cylinder, p. 46
lines: Here's step three in the book's photo: support hand under the trigger guard, thumb on the cylinder.

lines.text: On the drawing, release the catch.
The cylinder swings out on the crane, and you keep it controlled.
Load the ammunition into the chambers.
Then make sure the cylinder is locked in place.

scenes.heading: Unloading the revolver
bullets: Identify a safe direction
Safe direction, finger off the trigger
Left hand under guard, thumb on release catch
Open the cylinder, two fingers through frame
Remove ammunition: depress the ejector rod
lines: Page forty seven gives the steps for unloading.

lines.text: Step one: identify a safe direction.
Step two: point the firearm in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger.
Step three: place your left hand under the trigger guard and your right thumb on the cylinder release catch, with your trigger finger off the trigger.
Step four: open the cylinder, ensuring that your middle two fingers are on the cylinder and through the frame of the revolver.

lines: Your middle two fingers and thumb now have control of the cylinder.

lines.text: Step five: remove the ammunition from the cylinder by depressing the ejector rod.

scenes.heading: Step four
scenes.caption: Unloading, step 4: control the cylinder, p. 47
lines: In this photo, the middle two fingers and thumb control the open cylinder.

lines.text: Your right thumb goes on the cylinder release catch.
Open the cylinder.
And depress the ejector rod to remove the ammunition.

scenes.heading: Left-handed loading
scenes.caption: Loading the revolver for a left handed person, steps 1 to 5, p. 48
lines: Although the revolver is designed for right-handed people, the book gives a technique to help left-handed shooters load it correctly.
Pages forty eight and forty nine show it in eleven steps.

scenes.heading: Loading: left handed
bullets: Safe direction, finger off the trigger
Right thumb on cylinder release catch
Right index finger pushes cylinder out
Push your thumb through the frame
Grasp extractor rod like a cigarette
Close right hand around the cylinder
Load the cylinder
Left hand grips, right hand closes cylinder
Make sure the cylinder is locked in place
Complete the two handed grip
The revolver is now ready to be fired

lines.text: Step one: keep the revolver pointed in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger.
Step two: place the right thumb on the cylinder release catch.
Step three: push the cylinder out using the index finger of the right hand.

lines: Leave the trigger finger of the left hand in place to stop the cylinder from falling open.
It is opened by controlling it with the trigger finger of the left hand.

lines.text: Step four: push your thumb through the frame.
Step five: grasp the extractor rod in a similar manner to holding a cigarette.
Step six: close the right hand around the cylinder.
Step seven: load the cylinder.
Step eight: replace the grip with the gun hand, your left hand, while closing the cylinder with the right hand.
Step nine: make sure the cylinder is locked in place.
Step ten: complete the two handed grip.
Step eleven: the revolver is now ready to be fired.

scenes.caption: Loading the revolver for a left handed person, steps 6 to 11, p. 49
lines: Here are steps six to eleven in the book's photos.

scenes.heading: Left-handed unloading
scenes.caption: Unloading the revolver for a left handed person, p. 50
lines: Page fifty shows unloading for a left-handed person, in three steps.

scenes.heading: Unloading: left handed
bullets: Safe direction, open the cylinder
Thumb through frame, fingers on ejector rod
Right hand pushes the ejector rod
lines: Step one: with the firearm pointed in a safe direction, open the cylinder.
Step two: insert your thumb through the frame, placing the fingers onto the ejector rod.
Step three: with the right hand, push the ejector rod to eject the ammunition from the cylinder.

scenes.question: While loading, the cylinder can be rotated with the…
lines: You're loading ammunition into the chambers.
What can the cylinder be rotated with?
reveal: The thumb. The cylinder can be rotated with the thumb while loading.

scenes.question: How do you remove the ammunition when unloading?
lines: The cylinder is open.
How do you remove the ammunition?
reveal: Remove the ammunition from the cylinder by depressing the ejector rod.

points: Load the chambers, rotate with the thumb
Make sure the cylinder is locked in place
Left handed: right hand opens, closes, ejects
lines: Every procedure starts with the firearm pointed in a safe direction.
Load the chambers, rotating the cylinder with your thumb.
Make sure the cylinder is locked in place.
To unload, open the cylinder and depress the ejector rod.
And left-handed, the right hand pushes the cylinder out, closes it, and pushes the ejector rod.
